reference_title: Design and Construction of Driven Pile Foundations

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: 2015 update of the FHWA driven pile manual (supersedes 1985/1997/2006 editions), revised to incorporate LRFD methodology per AASHTO. Key updates include soil setup quantification, improved equipment monitoring, higher-strength materials, instrumented load tests, and enhanced QA/QC methods.
sections.body: In 1985 the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) published the first edition of this manual. Subsequent editions were published in 1997 and 2006. This 2015 update is primarily dictated by the need to revise and update manual content in accordance with the Load and Resistance Factor Design (LRFD) methodology which replaced the Allowable Strength Design (ASD) method for the design of transportation substructures in 2007.
key_points: Emphasis on rational economic evaluation of foundation design
Use of higher strength pile materials and/or larger driven pile sections
Updates in computer programs for pile foundation analysis and design
Use and quantification of soil setup in pile design and construction
Improvements in pile installation equipment and equipment performance monitoring
Increased use of instrumented static load test programs
Improvements in QA/QC methods for nominal resistance and pile integrity verifications
sections.applicability: General introduction to the GEC-12 manual and changes from previous editions.

sections.title: Purpose of the Manual
sections.summary: Compiles rational LRFD design procedures for driven pile foundations for all transportation projects. Replaces overly conservative historical methods; targets 15%+ substructure cost savings. Addresses complex loading: lateral, uplift, group behavior, and seismic events.
sections.body: The manual compiles proven rational design procedures, construction information, and useful case histories for driven pile foundations. It provides guidance for LRFD methodology applied to all transportation projects. Key purposes include: consolidating fragmented information, replacing overly conservative historical methods with rational approaches, enabling 15%+ substructure cost savings, providing comprehensive LRFD-based guidance, and addressing complex loading including lateral, uplift, group behavior, and seismic events.
key_points: Consolidates fragmented driven pile information for practicing engineers
Replaces overly conservative historical methods with rational design procedures
Minimum 15% substructure cost savings possible through improved methods
Comprehensive LRFD-based driven pile foundation manual
Addresses complex loading: lateral, uplift, group behavior, seismic events
Combined bending and axial load analysis required for modern pile design
Cost evaluation should be part of pile design selection
Larger selection of pile hammer types and sizes now available
sections.applicability: All driven pile foundation projects for highway structures.

sections.title: Scope of Manual
sections.summary: Limited to driven piles only (not drilled shafts, CFA piles, or micropiles). 18 chapters and 4 appendices across two volumes: Vol I (FHWA-NHI-16-009) covers design; Vol II (FHWA-NHI-16-010) covers resistance verification, equipment, and inspection.
sections.body: The manual is limited to driven piles and consists of eighteen chapters and four appendices across two volumes. Volume I (FHWA-NHI-16-009) covers the design aspects: cost evaluations, geotechnical data collection and analysis, selection of pile type, geotechnical and structural aspects of limit state design. Volume II (FHWA-NHI-16-010) covers methods of nominal resistance verification, pile driving equipment, accessories, and inspection procedures.
key_points: Limited to driven piles only (not drilled shafts, micropiles, or CFA piles)
18 chapters and 4 appendices across two volumes
Volume I: design aspects (cost, geotech data, pile type, limit state design)
Volume II: resistance verification, equipment, accessories, inspection
Theoretical discussions included only where necessary
Specific recommendations and example problems provided
sections.applicability: Defines the scope and organization of the two-volume manual.

sections.title: History of Driven Pile Foundations
sections.summary: Driven timber piles date to 800 BC. Reinforced concrete piles debuted 1897–1901; prestressed concrete cylinder piles in 1950s. Steam hammers patented 1839, diesel hammers developed mid-1920s Germany, vibratory hammers (Soviet origin) in U.S. 1960s, hydraulic hammers from Scandinavia 1960s.
sections.body: Earliest use of driven timber piles dates back to 800 BC using mauls or drop hammers. Reinforced concrete piles debuted in Europe in 1897 and Chicago in 1901. Structural steel piles (pipe, I-beams, H-piles) followed. Prestressed concrete piles as well as 36 and 54 inch diameter post-tensioned concrete cylinder piles developed in the 1950s. Steam pile hammers were patented in 1839. Diesel hammers were invented in Germany in the mid 1920s. Vibratory hammers from the Soviet Union appeared in U.S. markets in the 1960s. Hydraulic hammers developed in Scandinavia in the 1960s.
key_points: Driven timber piles date back to 800 BC
Reinforced concrete piles: Europe 1897, Chicago 1901
Prestressed concrete and cylinder piles developed in the 1950s
Steam hammers patented 1839, diesel hammers mid-1920s
Vibratory hammers from Soviet Union, U.S. market 1960s
Hydraulic hammers developed in Scandinavia 1960s
sections.applicability: Historical context for driven pile foundation practice.

sections.title: Information Sources
sections.summary: Primary reference: AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications 7th Ed. (2014) with 2015 Interim Revisions. Key supporting references: GEC-5 (Soil & Rock Properties), GEC-10 (Drilled Shafts), GEC-3 (LRFD Seismic), and HEC-18 (Scour at Bridges).
sections.body: Primary references are the 7th Edition of AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications (2014) with 2015 Interim Revisions and the 3rd Edition of AASHTO LRFD Bridge Construction Specifications. Additional sources include GEC-5 (Evaluation of Soil and Rock Properties), GEC-10 (Drilled Shafts), GEC-3 (LRFD Seismic Analysis), and HEC-18 (Evaluating Scour at Bridges).
key_points: AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 7th Edition (2014)
AASHTO LRFD Bridge Construction Specifications, 3rd Edition
GEC-5: Evaluation of Soil and Rock Properties (Sabatini et al. 2002)
GEC-10: Drilled Shafts (Brown et al. 2010)
GEC-3: LRFD Seismic Analysis (Kavazanjian et al. 2011)
HEC-18: Evaluating Scour at Bridges (Arneson et al. 2012)
